outcome.technical: (1) plugins/audit/hooks/_config.py: audit_config_way now asks a list of candidate trees that does not depend on where the path resolves to: the tree tree_for placed the path in (when inside), the project, the session's tree (_session_tree: a walk up to the project for a repository when the session stands under it elsewhere, path_tree's linked worktree when outside), and the config-shaped directory off the path once resolved (only inside the placed tree) and as written (only inside the placed tree or spelled under the project). Each is asked once by resolved directory (_candidate_word), an error costing that candidate only. config_question(tree, written, data) carries the written path and the session's cwd beside tree_for's answer; a relative path is also joined with the session's cwd. _names_audit_config compares resolved against resolved: identity where both exist, as before; for a creating write the config's folder and file are resolved first (_config_resolved, each followed where it is a link) and the resolved write is walked from the directory the folder resolves into, against the resolved names (_case_walk gains an owns parameter, default CONFIG_REL's parts). tree_for is NOT touched. (2) guard-edits.py rule 7 and the MCP lane ask the question of a path outside every tree too, the verdict naming the written path when there is no rel. (3) journal-writes.py: a write placed outside every tree that the question names is a config.edit row, target rel_path(project, path); the inside branch passes the written path too; no existing target changes. (4) SECURITY.md, plugins/audit/README.md, CHANGELOG.md, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md say what is matched through a symlink and what is not; no row of SECURITY.md's fail-mode table changed. (5) Tests: the property table (39 arrangements) is red before (18 of 38 agree on HEAD's hooks with the final table before ln39 was added; 15 of 31 at first) and 39 of 39 after. Verdicts of the orchestrator's probes, run on copies under the scratchpad: probe_j both writes block (the probe writes the file itself whatever the verdict, so its load line reads planGate off either way) and the journal row now exists; probe_g all three rows block/ask; probe_a 1960 runs, 0 differing verdicts or words; probe_c one changed step and 2/2 trail rows, the same as an export-vs-export control run (a fixture-name artifact in a tmp-alias target), 0 guard/journal disagreements; probe_f every change is allow to block/ask where the write creates the config, none the other way, 0 images attached after; the orchestrator's mine.py, mine2.py, probe_hold.py, probe5.py print identical output on the export and the tree. Disk calls of an ordinary write per kind (cf29 prints them), before the change and after: existing source file lstat 21 stat 2 -> lstat 21 stat 2; new source file lstat 21 stat 1 -> lstat 23 stat 1; config-named file in a plain folder lstat 21 stat 2 -> lstat 23 stat 2; no listing (cf29b). A session standing elsewhere than the project adds a walk up to the project, or outside it the path_tree git question. bench-hooks --gate exit 0 on 3.14.7 and on 3.9.6 (11 hooks within budget each). Unresolvable link: a dangling link resolves to the place it names and is matched there; a link that cannot be followed (a loop) resolves to the same unresolved spelling as the config's and is held as before, fail-closed (ln32 pins it; the mutation reading it as no file is caught). Deviation from the description: the project being always a candidate, a hard link to the project's config placed in an outside worktree is now held by identity (it IS the project's config); the documents say it is matched rather than listing it as not matched. The symlink FILE residual stays unmatched (ln38 pins it) and the shell route is unchanged. Mutation probe: 14 rows, MUTATIONS ALL CAUGHT, exit 0. Dependants: every hook importing _config keeps its behaviour except guard-edits and journal-writes as above (test_hooks 247, test_require_plan 245, test_guard_bash_writes 239, test__journal_io 276, test__config 413 cases all ok); the scripts reaching _config's loader do not call the changed functions; the documents listed are updated where they spoke of the config question and otherwise untouched.
